title: A local ring with a single prime ideal and separably closed residue field is strictly henselian
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring whose only prime ideal is $\mathfrak m$ (a local ring of Krull dimension $0$, e.g. an Artinian local ring), and suppose that the residue field $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$ is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed]. Then $R$ is strictly henselian in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]: for every finite $R$-algebra $B$ every idempotent of $B/\mathfrak mB$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $B$, and $\kappa$ is separably closed.

source.place: Lemma Tag 06RS (lemma-local-dimension-zero-henselian: local rings of dimension zero are henselian) and its proof: for R -> S finite, S has finitely many primes, all over m (Lemma Tag 05DR, lemma-finite-finite-fibres), no inclusions among them (Lemma Tag 00GT, lemma-integral-no-inclusion), so all maximal; their intersection is the nilradical (lemma-Zariski-topology), so S is the product of its localizations (Lemma Tag 00JA, lemma-product-local); a product of local rings lifts idempotents (Lemma Tag 04GG (10)=>(1), done in lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting step 5). The strict part is the hypothesis on kappa (Definition Tag 04GF).

proof.text: Convert ringKrullDim R = 0 to Ring.KrullDimLE 0 R with Ring.krullDimLE_iff. Mathlib Ring.KrullDimLE.nilradical_eq_maximalIdeal identifies m with the nilradical. For any R-algebra B, Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap and IsNilpotent.map imply mB is contained in nilradical B. This is a direct ideal-containment proof and does not require finiteness of B.

source.place: Dimension-zero hypothesis; Mathlib.RingTheory.KrullDimension.Zero and nilradical functoriality

proof.text: The quotient map B -> B/mB is surjective and has kernel mB. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotents-locally-nilpotent], namely Mathlib existsUnique_isIdempotentElem_eq_of_ker_isNilpotent, using step 1. This proves unique lifting for every algebra B, including the zero algebra and algebras in the independent universe v.

The maximal ideal is contained in the nilradical by step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-of-nil-maximal-ideal], which establishes the defining simple-root lifting property directly by finite Newton iteration. No idempotent/root-lifting equivalence is needed.

Combine HenselianLocalRing R with the assumed separably closed residue field using isStrictlyHenselianLocalRing_iff_henselianLocalRing_and_isSepClosed, the definition [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Pair this with step 2 in the independent universe v.

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks 06RS: step 1 (finitely many primes, all maximal over m, intersection nil: Stacks 05DR/00GT/00E0) is the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum (Algebra.QuasiFinite.discreteTopology_primeSpectrum with PrimeSpectrum.unique_of_ringKrullDimLE_zero and discreteTopology_iff_finite_and_krullDimLE_zero); step 2 (Stacks 00JA) is the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-product-of-localizations-at-maximal (MaximalSpectrum.toPiLocalizationEquiv, tagged @[stacks 00JA]); steps 3-4 (04GG (10)=>(1): reduction of a product of local rings is factorwise, idempotents are 0/1-vectors, lift uniquely) are written out as elementary, since lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting has this argument only inside its step 5, not as a node; step 5 is the hypothesis on kappa. No DAG node existed for 05DR, 00GT or 00JA. Statement unchanged. Alternative found: Mathlib's existsUnique_isIdempotentElem_eq_of_ker_isNilpotent (Stacks 00J9) with m = nilradical gives the idempotent clause directly (recorded in mathlib_searches). The slopmaster2 source has no HenselianLocalRing instance for Artinian or dimension-zero rings (only HenselianRing.bot, HenselianLocalRing.of_exists_algHom_comap_maximalIdeal_eq, HenselianLocalRing.of_isSepClosed_fractionRing, all sorry-free; Lean's HenselianLocalRing is the root-lifting form, equal to the idempotent form only through lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting).
